clue.text: 8 with trip, I flaunt dreadfully …

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 8 Down, AFFECTED, meaning showy and pretentious

parts.note: a drug trip is a high

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters of I FLAUNT are done badly, that is, jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone showing off on a holiday, flaunting themselves dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' points to the answer at 8 Down, which is the definition. 'dreadfully' gives the anagram of I flaunt, the second part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Highfalutin speech or manners are pompous and showy, which is the sense of affected here.

clue.text: Instrumental recording, set in regular three-four, on Light originally

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
set in says one piece goes inside the other
regular says every other letter of three-four is taken

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: originally says only the first letter of Light is used

explanation.surface: An instrumental record in waltz time, played on a light programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular' takes every other letter of three-four, and 'set in' puts the record inside them. 'Instrumental' suggests music, but it means useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being instrumental in something means playing a useful part in it, so helpful.

clue.text: Sports periodical turns up on Wednesdays — central points being significant

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above
in a down clue, turns up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a periodical

indicators.note: only the central points of the word count, so its middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A sports magazine that comes out on Wednesdays, where the key points matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reads MAG upwards as GAM; 'central points being significant' takes ES, the middle of WEDNESDAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Games are sports, as in the Olympic Games or games lessons at school.

clue.text: Barred door at front opening on behalf of US President

parts.note: acting for someone is acting on their behalf

indicators.note: the president's name is opened up to take the other piece inside

parts.note: Joe Biden was US President when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: at front says only the first letter of door is used

explanation.surface: A door barred at the front entrance on the President's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front' gives D from door; 'opening' puts it inside BIDEN to make BIDDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred means prohibited or not allowed, which is forbidden.

clue.text: Put bar on attendance? That'll control the flow

parts.note: to lock a door is to put a bar on it
the gate is the number of people attending a match

explanation.surface: Barring people from attending, which will control the flow of crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: GATE is the British word for the crowd attending a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock gate on a canal holds back or releases water to regulate its movement.

clue.text: They left bequests of property, within limits of 'thriftiness'

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an estate is a piece of property

explanation.surface: Thrifty people who left bequests of property within careful limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of' gives T and S from thriftiness, and 'within' puts ESTATE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate is a person who died having made a valid will, so who left bequests.

clue.text: Material from river reportedly turning up negative

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Cloth from a river, apparently, with a negative result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns NILE into its sound-alike NYL; 'turning up' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a kind of cloth material.

clue.text: Obscure novel found in various syllabuses — first half of work's dashed off

indicators.note: various says the letters of syllabuses come in a different order
dashed off says those letters are struck out of the mix
first half of says only the opening half of the word is kept

parts.note: labour is work

explanation.surface: A difficult novel turns up on many reading lists, though half the work is skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' takes LAB from LABOUR; 'dashed off' removes it from SYLLABUSES, and 'various' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses by James Joyce is a famously difficult modernist novel, often called obscure.

clue.text: Disturbed very loudly, elephant's head moved about

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: acted means moved, as in took action
ff, fortissimo, is the music notation for very loudly

indicators.note: head says only the first letter of elephant is used

explanation.surface: An elephant disturbed by loud noise, tossing its head about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the word for moved around the musical mark plus the elephant's first letter; 'head' picks that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be affected by something is to be moved or upset by it, so disturbed.

clue.text: … silly poems with mostly tired, vacuous kookiness about Morecambe

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go around the next one
mostly says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: tired and floppy means limp

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outer letters of kookiness remain

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Across: daft verses, tired and kooky, about the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly', 'vacuous' and 'about' are the indicators. Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it is the British comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Limericks are comic five-line verses, the classic example of nonsense poetry.

clue.text: 8 left from outskirts of Torquay

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 8 Down, AFFECTED, in its haughty sense

parts.note: of can mean from, as in coming of good stock

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone leaving the edge of the Devon resort of Torquay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' takes the first and last letters of Torquay, T and Y. Torquay is a seaside town in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty manners are haughty and superior, the airs of someone affected.

clue.text: Console female attached to Isaac, having broken up

indicators.note: broken up says the letters of Isaac are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Comforting a woman attached to Isaac after their break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like a verb, to comfort; it is a noun, the dashboard panel. 'having broken up' rearranges ISAAC into ASCIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is the dashboard of a car, the panel of controls also called a console.

clue.text: Graduate, falling short and beginning to stagnate, grumbles

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree
falling short of a mark means under it

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of stagnate is used

explanation.surface: A graduate whose career falls short and stagnates, and who complains about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is an old word for to grumble or mutter on aimlessly.

clue.text: 8 young man married to Gilbert's royal daughter

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 8 Down, AFFECTED, as in genteel and pretentious

parts.note: a lad is a young man
Princess Ida is the title character of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, a king's daughter

explanation.surface: A young man wed to the princess of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'married to' simply joins the two pieces. Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes a pretentiously refined manner, which is affected behaviour.

clue.text: No longer working after cutback, climbing with kids inside racing car

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes into the other
in a down clue, climbing means the word reads bottom to top
cut back to its abbreviation, the word loses its middle letters

parts.note: someone no longer working is retired
to kid someone is to rag or tease them

explanation.surface: A retired driver after cutbacks, climbing into a racing car with the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cutback' shortens the word to the abbreviation RETD, 'climbing' turns that into DTER, and 'inside' puts the kids in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing, short sprints down a straight strip.

clue.text: Almost worn-out aboard negligently used junk

indicators.note: aboard says one piece goes inside the other, as on a ship
done negligently, the letters of used fall out of order
almost says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a worn-out phrase is trite

explanation.surface: Something nearly worn out, carelessly used, and now junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negligently' scrambles the clue's 'used' into DEUS, 'Almost' shortens the synonym, and 'aboard' puts it inside DEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or rubbish left behind, which is junk.

clue.text: Back Red in production of larger hit

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of the letters of larger hit

explanation.surface: A backing singer in a production of a larger hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear light is the red lamp at the back of a vehicle.

clue.text: Unchanged pitch is minute and impossible, given Yorkshire's tail

parts.note: MO, short for moment, is a minute
something not on is not possible

indicators.note: tail says only the last letter of Yorkshire is used

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch in Yorkshire, unchanged and unplayable at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT ON is British for out of the question. 'pitch' looks like a Yorkshire cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotone is a voice or sound that stays on one note, without change of tone.

clue.text: Change from modest shilling

parts.note: modest and unadorned means plain
a bob is old British slang for a shilling, the pre-decimal coin

explanation.surface: Some small change from a modest shilling coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like money, but it is a change in bell-ringing. BOB is British slang for a shilling, an old coin worth five pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain Bob is a basic method in change ringing, the English art of ringing church bells in sequences.

clue.text: 8 old politician's in soup, unfortunately

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 8 Down, AFFECTED, as in self-important

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
unfortunately says the letters of soup end up in a bad state, jumbled

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An old politician in the soup, meaning in trouble, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'politician's' reads as 'politician is'. 'unfortunately' makes POUS from SOUP, and 'in' puts OMP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompous person is self-important and pretentious, which is the affected manner.

clue.text: Space vehicle, coming from star, disappears

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spaceship emerging from a star before vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The TARDIS is the time and space machine flown by the Doctor in the TV series Doctor Who.

clue.text: Saws sharpened accurately to begin with by Yankee in outskirts of Gallipolis

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
to begin with says only the first letters of those words are used

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters of Gallipolis

explanation.surface: Saws being sharpened by an American in a town called Gallipolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saws' looks like tools; here they are proverbs. 'outskirts of' gives GS from Gallipolis, a town in Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, so saws are sayings.

clue.text: Interference having scope to proliferate

parts.note: mush is radio jargon for background interference or noise
scope to do something is room to do it

explanation.surface: Interference that is given free scope will multiply.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or spread rapidly, like fungi springing up overnight.

clue.text: Hoist in preparation for delivery

definitions.meaning: to ... a flag is to hoist it
a bowler's ... in cricket comes before the ball is delivered

explanation.surface: Lifting goods ready to send them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Run up means raise, as of a flag; a run-up is the approach a cricket bowler makes before bowling.

clue.text: Desirable type of 8 voice …

definitions.meaning: a ... job is a choice, desirable one
a ... voice is a posh, affected accent, 8 Down being AFFECTED

explanation.surface: Continuing into the next clue: an attractive kind of affected voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Plummy means rich and choice, and also describes an upper-class, plum-in-the-mouth accent.

clue.text: Dance with Mike on platform in church

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ambo is a raised stand or pulpit in an early church

explanation.surface: Dancing with a man called Mike on a church platform.
explanation.definitionFit: The mambo is a lively Latin American dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: See 4
… in performance by Lyric Theatre

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: Continuing 23 Across: a voice heard in a show at the Lyric Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric is a London theatre, but here 'Lyric' is a lyric poem, ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a name used for theatres and especially cinemas, from the Greek word for a concert hall.

clue.text: Member marching in order of age, Norman? Not exactly!

indicators.note: not exactly AGE NORMAN, but an inexact arrangement of those letters

explanation.surface: A man called Norman marching in order of age, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like 'in sequence'; it is the Orange Order. 'Not exactly' rearranges AGE NORMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orangeman belongs to the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland famous for its marches.

clue.text: Papa keeping final letter under wraps (before the Telegraph becomes 8?)

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 8 Down, AFFECTED, in the sense of showy

indicators.note: before says the piece comes ahead of the next one

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the final letter is kept under wraps, so the last letter of the word is hidden away and dropped

parts.note: keeping or holding on to something is retention
the newspaper speaking of itself says we or us; this puzzle is in the Telegraph

explanation.surface: A father keeping his last letter secret before the newspaper turns pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final letter under wraps' hides the last letter of the word for keeping. A newspaper refers to itself in the first person plural, and this puzzle ran in the Telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious behaviour claims more importance or refinement than is due, which is the affected manner.
